blocks.h2: Does Your Geneva Sewer Line Need Regular Service?

tiles.body: Many historic blocks have trees older than the sewer line. Roots return to the same joints every year.
Clay lines from the 1800s and early 1900s have a joint every few feet.
One backup can cost more than many years of maintenance.

blocks.h2: How Often Geneva Lines Need Service
blocks.intro: Older lines usually need more attention. Here's where most homes land:
head: Your Line
Typical Interval
rows: Original clay under a historic home
Root cutting every year, before spring
Cast iron inside an older home
Jetting every couple of years to keep scale down
A camera check every year or two at the transitions
PVC line in a newer home
A camera look every few years

blocks.intro: In September 2008, about 9 inches of rain fell on Geneva in two days, and basements flooded across much of Kane County.

items.h3: Root Control in the Historic District
items.body: In the Central Geneva Historic District, roots are the main reason lines need regular service. A yearly cleaning keeps them from closing the pipe.
In September 2008, about 9 inches of rain fell in two days. A line already half full of roots has no room left in a storm like that.
If you have a backflow valve or an [overhead sewer system](/geneva/overhead-sewer-systems), we check it on the same visit.

blocks.h2: What a Maintenance Visit Can (and Can't) Fix
blocks.intro: A maintenance visit is built around prevention, not repair. Here's where the line falls:
head: Included in a Maintenance Visit
Needs a Different Service
rows: A camera inspection to check your line's current condition
An active sewage backup. Likely fix: [Emergency Plumbing](/geneva/emergency-plumbing)
Catching early root growth or wear before it becomes a bigger problem
A cracked or collapsed pipe. Likely fix: [Sewer Repair](/geneva/sewer-repair)
A light interior clean as part of the visit
A heavy clog that needs full clearing. Likely fix: [Sewer Rodding](/geneva/sewer-rodding) or [Hydro Jetting](/geneva/hydro-jetting)
An honest assessment of what your line needs next
A line at the end of its lifespan. Likely fix: [Trenchless Sewer Repair](/geneva/trenchless-sewer-repair)
blocks.note: If your line needs more than a checkup, we'll tell you exactly what and why. No surprise upsells.

steps.body: We record it end to end and note every joint and patch.
Root cutting for clay joints, jetting for scale and grease.
Interval and price in writing before the next visit is booked.

blocks.h2: Sewer Maintenance Questions From Geneva Homeowners

items.q: Why does my historic home need sewer service every year?
items.preview: Clay joints and old trees mean roots come back yearly.
items.answer: Clay lines have a joint every few feet, and old trees send roots into them every growing season. Cutting them back each year keeps the line open.

items.q: Can a liner end the yearly cleanings?
items.preview: Often, yes. It seals the joints roots use.
items.answer: Often. A [trenchless liner](/geneva/trenchless-sewer-repair) seals every joint, so roots have no way in. Many homeowners line the pipe after a few years of yearly cleanings.

items.preview: It helps, but a full public sewer needs other protection.
items.answer: A clean line carries water out faster. When the public sewer itself is full, you need a backflow valve or an [overhead sewer system](/geneva/overhead-sewer-systems).

items.q: Is sewer maintenance part of the No Drip Club?
items.preview: The No Drip Club includes regular maintenance visits.
items.answer: The [No Drip Club](/no-drip-club/) brings a plumber to your home for regular maintenance. Ask how it applies to your sewer line.

items.q: How much does sewer maintenance cost in Geneva?
items.preview: It depends on the service. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on whether your line needs root cutting, jetting or a camera check. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
